albums.blurb: Piazzolla was the Argentine bandoneonist and composer who spent four decades transforming tango into nuevo tango, folding in jazz improvisation and classical form over fierce resistance from Buenos Aires traditionalists. Recorded in New York in May 1986 with his Quinteto Tango Nuevo — bandoneon, violin, piano, electric guitar, and double bass — and produced by Kip Hanrahan for the American Clavé label, Zero Hour opens the late-career trilogy that capped his half-century of work, and its seven pieces are entirely instrumental.
albums.reception: Piazzolla himself declared it "absolutely the greatest record I've made in my entire life," and Rolling Stone likened its fusion of form, improvisation, and dynamics to contemporary classical music, jazz, and rock & roll.

albums.blurb: The Marías are a Los Angeles band built around Puerto Rican-born singer María Zardoya and drummer-producer Josh Conway, singing in both English and Spanish. Submarine is their second studio album, following CINEMA (2021); Zardoya and Conway ended their long relationship after the CINEMA tour, took a six-month hiatus, and then wrote this water-themed record about the breakup, giving it a lonelier, more cinematic cast than their earlier work.
albums.reception: Submarine debuted at No. 17 on the Billboard 200 — the band's highest-charting album to date — and its single "No One Noticed" later climbed to No. 22 on the Hot 100.

albums.blurb: Souls of Mischief are the Oakland four-piece of A-Plus, Opio, Phesto, and Tajai, part of the Hieroglyphics collective founded with Del the Funky Homosapien. This debut, released on Jive in September 1993 and recorded at San Francisco's Hyde Street Studios, set jazz- and funk-sampling production (largely handled in-house) under a rapid tag-team rhyme style — a laid-back, lyric-first alternative to the G-funk then dominating California rap, with the title track becoming the group's signature song.
albums.reception: The album reached No. 85 on the Billboard 200 and No. 17 on the Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart, and in 1998 The Source selected it as one of its 100 Best Rap Albums.
